tasks.subject: Decide host-hash recipe (single-source vs multi-source)
tasks.description:
DECIDED. The recipe is single-source primary with fallback chain (product_uuid → machine_id → hostname), 12-hex SHA256, kind-prefixed in the salt. My lean was accepted (the PoC and slice 1 implementation both confirm it). The c2c-side validator at `ocaml/c2c_name.ml` widens to 12-16 hex for a cheap escape hatch but the canonical recipe is 12.

Why single-source: stability. If the hostname changes, the alias must NOT change (the old alias would orphan). Combining sources amplifies churn: change any one source and the hash changes. We accept lower entropy in exchange for stability.

Why 12 hex: ~10⁻⁶ collision at 1M hosts, acceptable for the relay scale. Widened to 16 hex (64 bits, ~10⁻¹⁰ at 1M) in the validator for a future escape hatch.

Why no MAC: pi-313d8c feedback — MACs are unreliable, expose OUI, need elevated perms.

Recipe parity PROVEN: `c2c host-id` returns `3d08761ae3f3` on this machine, matching the extension's `pi-c2c/src/relay.ts:computeHostHash()`. PoC at `ocaml/tools/host_id_poc.ml` is the recipe-parity reference. Production code at `ocaml/host_id.ml` uses digestif (no shell-out).

tasks.subject: Hybrid followUp → triggerTurn promotion (if needed)
tasks.description:
The drain-bug-is-followup-delay finding documented that followUp messages can wait up to 4.5 minutes during long turns. Mitigations include a hybrid that promotes queued messages to `triggerTurn: true` after a threshold (e.g. 30s).

Don't implement yet — observe whether the lag is actually a UX problem. If it is, the change is ~10 lines in `pi-c2c/src/delivery.ts`:
1. Track `queuedSince` per followUp message
2. In pollTick, when a message is queued for >N seconds, switch the delivery options to `{ triggerTurn: true }` on the next tick
3. Reset the queuedSince once the message is delivered

Alternative: just always use `triggerTurn: true` (c2c messages are important; agent can resume). Cost: interrupts user investigations.

tasks.subject: PoC: OCaml port of computeHostHash for recipe parity
tasks.description:
Port the extension's computeHostHash() to OCaml and verify byte-for-byte parity on this machine. Required before any c2c-side opaque_host_id implementation to prevent the "alias changes on migration" failure mode.

Steps:
1. Write OCaml program that implements the same recipe: try /sys/class/dmi/id/product_uuid → /etc/machine-id → hostname, hash with sha256("<kind>=<value>")[:12]
2. Compile and run on this machine (xsm, machine_id=f59bb56bdbc74dc9a151ad27fdd4a94d, product_uuid not readable)
3. Compare OCaml output to extension's reported host_hash (3d08761ae3f3)
4. If match: recipe parity confirmed, document in design doc, slice 1 can proceed
5. If mismatch: pin down the spec (whitespace, encoding, hostname split), re-port

Status: in progress, debugging OCaml Unix module linkage.

tasks.description:

- Add `opaque_host_id: string option` to `RegistrationLease` record in `ocaml/relay.ml`

tasks.subject: Implement c2c slice 2: extension consumes opaque_host_id
tasks.description:
Slice 2 of the opaque_host_id design (.collab/design/2026-06-17-c2c-opaque-host-id.md, commit 44c6b512). Slice 1 (c2c-side) is landed in `3d37905c`. Now the extension picks up the new field.

Current state:
- Extension already computes `computeHostHash()` (in `pi-c2c/src/relay.ts`) and uses `deriveRelayAlias(alias, hostHash)` to build `<alias>#<host_hash>` for the relay alias on `session_start` (see `src/index.ts:483-484`).
- c2c-side parses the `<name>#<hostid>` alias suffix into `opaque_host_id` on the lease (slice 1).

So the basic flow already works. Slice 2 is mostly:
1. **Verify end-to-end**: register on the relay via the new c2c binary (which has slice 1), check the resulting registration has `opaque_host_id = <host_hash>` populated, and `/list` returns it per peer.
2. **Consume `opaque_host_id` in c2c_pi_local_info**: show the field alongside the existing `host_hash` (which is the locally-computed one) so the user can see "what the relay has on file for me" vs "what my extension computed".
3. **Tests**: integration test that runs c2c with slice 1, registers a pi-c2c session, and asserts the relay list returns the opaque_host_id. Could be a new test in `tests/routing.test.ts` (the existing routing tests already use the C2cCli wrapper) or `tests/c2c-cli.test.ts`.

Status: pending, will pick up after swarm review of slice 1.

Open question for swarm: should the extension surface BOTH `host_hash` (locally-computed) and `opaque_host_id` (server-stored) in c2c_pi_local_info, or just one? Lean: both, since they can differ (e.g. if a different client registers from the same machine with a different recipe).
